h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: When the deep path into node 3 ends in a conv3x3, an identity shortcut on edge 3 forms a residual block that eases optimisation, matching the skip-on-edge-3 pattern of top NB201 cells.
With pooling at the start of the long path, edge 3 is one of few places learned capacity enters, so trading it for identity costs more.
When node 2 partly carries parameter-free pooled features, a learned conv on its only outgoing edge supplies capacity that would otherwise be missing.
When node 2 already receives a conv3x3 from edge 1, an additional conv3x3 on edge 2 shows diminishing returns.
A parallel conv3x3 on edge 3 already supplies spatial capacity into node 3, so a second conv on edge 4 is partly redundant.
Removing edge 2 destroys the deepest conv chain that a conv3x3 on edge 5 exploits, so the loss of depth is costlier.
With conv capacity supplied by edge 4 into node 3, a conv on edge 3 is redundant and an identity residual is the more valuable use of the edge.
Two pooling branches into node 2 leave it fully parameter-free and over-smoothed, so adding pooling on edge 1 hurts more.
An identity on edge 5 passes node-2 features straight to the output, which pays off when node 2 holds deep conv features from edge 2 rather than parameter-free ones.
An identity on edge 4 forwards node-1 features, which are useful learned features when edge 0 is a conv but only pooled or raw input otherwise.
